title: Where to Stay in Vrsar: 2027 Accommodation Guide
metaDescription: Discover the best areas to stay in Vrsar, Croatia. Compare Old Town apartments, waterfront hotels, family resorts, and naturist camps with 2027 prices.
content:
## Understanding Vrsar's Layout

Vrsar is a compact coastal town in Istria, Croatia, built on a prominent 54-meter-high hill that slopes down to the Adriatic Sea. The town oversees an archipelago of 18 uninhabited islands. Because of its distinct topography and historical development, Vrsar is divided into highly specific zones. Where you choose to stay dictates your daily routine: whether you will be walking up steep inclines, navigating through large resort complexes, or stepping directly onto flat harbor promenades.

The accommodation landscape in Vrsar is heavily dominated by Maistra Hospitality Group, which operates the major hotels, resorts, and campsites surrounding the town center. Independent accommodation is largely restricted to private apartment rentals in the Old Town and the residential streets immediately bordering the historic core.

## 1. Vrsar Old Town (Stari Grad)

The Old Town is the historical center of Vrsar, characterized by narrow, winding cobblestone streets, stone houses, and small squares. It sits at the highest point of the town, crowned by the Church of St. Martin and the abandoned residence of the Porec Bishops.

### Who Should Stay Here
The Old Town appeals to couples, history enthusiasts, and travelers looking for a traditional Mediterranean atmosphere. It provides excellent views of the harbor and the islands, particularly near the famous Casanova Viewpoint (named after Giacomo Casanova, who visited Vrsar in the 18th century).

### Accommodation Types and Prices
Lodging here consists almost entirely of private apartments, boutique guesthouses, and renovated stone villas. Hotel Vista is one of the few formal hotel options in this zone, offering rooms from €110 to €150 per night in the peak summer season. Private one-bedroom apartments generally range from €80 to €130 per night in July and August, dropping to €50 to €70 in the shoulder seasons of May and October.

### The Reality of Staying in the Old Town
The boutique apartments in the Old Town look charming online, but dragging heavy luggage up the steep, pedestrian-only cobblestone streets in July heat is a miserable way to start a vacation. Mobility is a serious factor here. The core of the Old Town is closed to non-resident traffic. If you rent an apartment near the top of the hill, you will likely need to park your car in the main Saline parking lot at the bottom of the town (costing around €10 to €15 per day) and carry your bags uphill. 

Daily grocery runs to the larger Plodine or Konzum supermarkets require walking down to the main road and hauling supplies back up. However, the reward is quiet evenings away from the noisy harbor bars and immediate access to traditional taverns like Caffe Bar Ladonja.

## 2. The Marina and Waterfront (Obala)

Directly below the Old Town sits Vrsar's modern marina and waterfront promenade. This area stretches from the town's main public beach (Gradska plaža) in the north to the edge of the Belvedere peninsula in the south.

### Who Should Stay Here
The waterfront is the best location for travelers who want flat, walkable access to restaurants, cafes, and boat excursions. It is ideal for visitors with limited mobility, families with young children in strollers, and those who want to be in the center of the town's evening activity.

### Accommodation Types and Prices
This area features a mix of standard hotels, aparthotels, and modern private rentals. Hotel Pineta is a prominent fixture overlooking the marina, offering indoor and outdoor pools with nightly rates around €140 to €190 during peak season. Apartments along the Obala Maršala Tita (the main waterfront street) command premium prices due to sea views, averaging €120 to €180 per night.

### Pros and Cons of the Waterfront
Staying at the marina puts you steps away from morning coffee, bakery runs, and dinner at well-regarded local restaurants like Konoba Trost. The departure points for boat tours to the nearby Lim Fjord are located right on the docks. 

The main drawback is noise. During the summer, Vrsar hosts regular fisherman's festivals (Ribarske fešte) and live music events on the promenade. If your accommodation faces the harbor, expect crowd noise and music until late in the evening. Additionally, the beaches directly adjacent to the marina can feel crowded, requiring a 10 to 15-minute walk south to Montraker beach or north to Valkanela for cleaner water and more space.

## 3. Belvedere and Petalon Peninsulas

Just south of the marina, the coastline extends into a series of small, heavily forested peninsulas. This is the territory of Vrsar's major resort complexes, specifically Resort Belvedere and Resort Petalon.

### Who Should Stay Here
These resort areas are designed for families, active travelers, and vacationers who prefer an all-in-one environment where swimming pools, beaches, sports facilities, and dining are located within a single complex.

### Accommodation Types and Prices
Resort Belvedere features terraced apartments built into the hillside, designed to give maximum units a sea view. It sits closest to the town center, making it easy to walk to the marina in under 10 minutes. Prices here average €160 to €220 per night for a family apartment in summer.

Petalon is situated slightly further south, just past the Montraker quarry (a historical site where stone was extracted for Venetian palaces). Petalon offers a mix of hotel rooms and apartments, with prices ranging from €130 to €200 per night. Both resorts are managed by Maistra and offer consistent, standardized amenities.

### Resort Area Amenities
Staying in the Belvedere or Petalon zones means you do not need a car for daily activities. The complexes feature paved pathways, bike rentals, tennis courts, and dedicated diving centers. The beaches here are classic Istrian: rocky shorelines equipped with concrete sunbathing plateaus, stainless steel ladders into the clear water, and pebble coves designed for children. Because these resorts handle high volumes of guests, the on-site restaurants can feel institutional, but the proximity to Vrsar's town center makes it easy to leave the resort for authentic local dining.

## 4. Koversada Naturist Park

Further south from Petalon lies Koversada, which requires its own specific category. Established in 1961, Koversada is one of the oldest and largest naturist (FKK - Freikörperkultur) resorts in Europe. It occupies a massive stretch of coastline and includes a small island connected to the mainland by a footbridge.

### Who Should Stay Here
Koversada is strictly for naturist travelers. While clothing is required in the shops and indoor restaurants, the beaches, campsites, and general outdoor areas are designated as clothing-optional or strict naturist zones.

### Accommodation Types and Prices
The complex is vast, capable of hosting thousands of guests. Accommodation is highly varied:
*   **Villas and Apartments:** Basic, functional masonry pavilions offering rooms and small apartments. Rates run €90 to €140 per night.
*   **Mobile Homes:** Modern mobile homes with air conditioning and private decks, usually priced between €130 and €180 per night.
*   **Camping Pitches:** Hundreds of plots for tents and RVs, averaging €40 to €70 per night depending on proximity to the sea.

### Inside Koversada
Koversada operates as an independent village. It contains its own supermarkets, bakeries, medical facilities, and multiple restaurants (such as Batana and Mendula). The beaches stretch for over 5 kilometers, featuring a mix of rocky outcrops, concrete terraces, and a large imported-sand beach (Blesička) which is highly popular with families. If you stay in Koversada, walking to Vrsar's main harbor takes 20 to 30 minutes, though many guests prefer to rent bicycles to navigate the large distances within the camp and into town.

## 5. Valkanela and the Northern Coast

North of Vrsar's town center, the landscape flattens out into a large bay shared with the neighboring municipality of Funtana. The Vrsar side of this bay is occupied by Camping Valkanela.

### Who Should Stay Here
Valkanela is aimed squarely at families who want a traditional outdoor resort experience without the naturist rules of Koversada. It is highly active, pet-friendly, and geared toward children and teenagers.

### Accommodation Types and Prices
While traditional tent and RV camping is available, the most popular accommodations here are the premium mobile homes. Many of these modern, prefabricated units feature multiple bedrooms, full kitchens, covered terraces, and access to shared or private small swimming pools. Prices for mobile homes in July and August run between €150 and €250 per night, reflecting high demand for self-contained family lodging.

### Valkanela Logistics
Valkanela features a massive central pool complex, trampoline parks, mini-golf, and extensive pebble beaches. The main drawback of staying in the Valkanela zone is the distance from Vrsar itself. The walk from the center of the Valkanela campsite to Vrsar's harbor is roughly 2.5 kilometers along a coastal path. While it is a flat, scenic walk, doing it multiple times a day with children is impractical. Visitors staying here usually rely on bicycles or drive their cars into the main Saline parking lot when they want to visit the Old Town.

## Seasonal Timing and Booking Strategy

Vrsar's accommodation operates on a strict seasonal schedule. The town is largely dormant from November through Easter. 

*   **Peak Season (July to August):** Prices are at their highest. Hotels and resorts frequently enforce minimum stay requirements of 3 to 5 nights. You must book at least four to six months in advance to secure specific mobile homes or Old Town apartments.
*   **Shoulder Season (May, June, September):** This is the optimal time to visit. Prices drop by 30% to 50%, the sea is generally warm enough for swimming by mid-June, and the temperatures are suitable for walking the steep hills of the Old Town. 
*   **Off-Season (October to April):** The large Maistra resorts and campsites close entirely. The only available accommodations are private apartments and a few independent guesthouses. Many local restaurants also shut down for the winter.

## Transportation and Parking Near Your Accommodation

When choosing your area in Vrsar, factor in your vehicle. If you book in the Belvedere, Petalon, Valkanela, or Koversada complexes, secure parking is provided on-site. 

If you book an apartment in the Old Town or along the Marina, parking is heavily regulated. The town uses a zoned parking system. You will likely have to use the large municipal lots (Saline or the lot near the bus station) and pay a daily rate of €10 to €15. Some private apartment owners include a prepaid parking card in their rental rate, so confirm this before booking.

faq.question: Do you need a car in Vrsar?
faq.answer: If you stay in the Old Town, the Marina, or the Belvedere resort, you do not need a car as restaurants, beaches, and supermarkets are within a 15-minute walk. However, a car is highly recommended if you want to explore the rest of Istria or if you stay further out in the Valkanela campsite.

faq.question: Is Vrsar a good place to stay for families?
faq.answer: Yes, Vrsar is excellent for families. The resort areas like Petalon, Belvedere, and Valkanela are specifically designed for children, offering safe pebble beaches, large swimming pools, and dedicated entertainment programs.

faq.question: Where is the best place to park if staying in the Vrsar Old Town?
faq.answer: The Old Town is mostly pedestrian-only. You will need to park at the large Saline parking lot located near the marina at the bottom of the hill. Expect to pay around €10 to €15 per day during the summer season.

faq.question: Are the beaches in Vrsar sandy?
faq.answer: No, Vrsar's natural beaches are predominantly rocky with pebbles or consist of paved concrete terraces. The only major sandy area is Blesička beach, an artificial sand beach located inside the Koversada naturist park.

faq.question: What is the difference between staying at Resort Belvedere and Resort Petalon?
faq.answer: Resort Belvedere is closer to the Vrsar town center and marina, making it easier to walk to local restaurants. Petalon is located slightly further south past the Montraker quarry, offering a quieter atmosphere and better access to dedicated sports facilities.

faq.question: Is Koversada strictly for naturists?
faq.answer: Yes, Koversada is a dedicated naturist (FKK) resort. While clothing is required inside shops and restaurants, guests are expected to adhere to naturist rules on the beaches and throughout the outdoor camping and residential areas.

quickAnswer: The best area to stay in Vrsar depends on your travel style. Choose the Old Town for historic charm, the Marina for dining and boat access, Petalon or Belvedere for family-friendly beach resorts, and Koversada for Europe's largest naturist camping experience.
